title: Influence of α-FeOOH and flow-driven particle suspension on aqueous PFOA during PFAS precursor chlorination
content: Chlorination can transform PFAS precursors into perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), but the role of iron particles in the aqueous-phase behavior of these compounds in drinking water distribution systems remains unclear. Particle suspension also changes with flow, making hydraulic conditions relevant to this process. We combined batch experiments with a pilot study to examine how α-FeOOH addition and flow-dependent particle suspension relate to aqueous PFOAAmS, PFOAB, and PFOA concentrations. After 24 h of batch chlorination, the α-FeOOH-containing system had lower aqueous precursor residues than the particle-free control, particularly for PFOAB (22.4%), while mean aqueous PFOA was modestly higher (4.6%). This difference occurred alongside changes in apparent particle size and dissolved organic matters, despite broadly comparable bulk free-chlorine decay. In the pilot study, greater suspended-Fe exposure at the higher tested velocities was accompanied by higher aqueous PFOA concentrations. Together, these results show that iron particles are relevant to the risks of PFAS during chlorination, and that their suspension under different hydraulic conditions accelerates PFOA production during distribution.
